faq.q: What is the sea temperature in Sotogrande in July?
faq.a: In July, the Mediterranean off Sotogrande typically reaches 22–24°C. That's warm enough for comfortable swimming, snorkelling, and paddleboarding. By late afternoon, the surface layer can feel even warmer, especially in shallow coves like Cala del Faro.

faq.q: How windy is it in Sotogrande in July?
faq.a: July winds are usually light to moderate, averaging 10–15 knots. The typical pattern is a gentle thermal breeze that builds from late morning and dies down by sunset. Occasionally, a levante (easterly) can bring stronger gusts, but these rarely last more than a day.

faq.q: Is July a good month for a yacht charter in Sotogrande?
faq.a: Yes, July offers the most reliable summer weather: long sunny days, warm seas, and minimal rain. The only downside is peak-season crowds, so book early and consider morning departures to avoid the busiest anchorages.

faq.q: What should I wear on a July yacht charter?
faq.a: Bring lightweight, breathable clothing, a swimsuit, a sun hat, and UV-protection sunglasses. Even though it's hot, a light windbreaker is useful for the breeze at sea. Don't forget reef-safe sunscreen with SPF 50+ and a rash guard for extra protection.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a July family charter in Sotogrande?
faq.a: For families, the Azimut 39 (11 pax) or Astondoa 40 (9 pax) offer comfortable shaded cockpits, a small galley, and easy swimming access. Both are perfect for a 4-hour coastal cruise from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande, with stops for snorkelling.

faq.q: Can I anchor and swim anywhere in July?
faq.a: You can anchor in most sandy coves, but always respect protected areas like the dunes at Cabopino. Popular spots include Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, and the waters off Sotogrande's beach. Your skipper will choose the calmest spot based on wind and tide.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a July charter?
faq.a: July is the busiest month, so aim to book at least 2–3 weeks ahead, especially for weekends. For the Mangusta 80 (which includes a free jet ski), we recommend 4–6 weeks' notice to secure your preferred date and departure time.

data.body_html:
Planning a Sotogrande yacht charter in July? You're picking the best month for guaranteed sunshine, warm seas, and long days on the water. With air temperatures hitting 28–32°C and sea water around 22–24°C, July delivers classic Mediterranean conditions. This guide covers everything you need to know about the weather, sea state, and how to make the most of your charter from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande.

July Weather in Sotogrande: What to Expect

July is the heart of summer on the Costa del Sol. Expect clear blue skies, very little rain (less than 5mm for the whole month), and humidity that stays manageable thanks to the sea breeze. The average high is 32°C, but it can feel warmer on the water without shade — so bring a hat and plenty of water (though your charter includes soft drinks and beer).

UV index is extreme (8–9), so reapply sunscreen every two hours, even if you're swimming. The sea breeze typically starts around 11:00, reaching 10–15 knots by mid-afternoon — perfect for sailing but slightly choppy for small boats. Plan your anchor stops for late morning or early afternoon for the calmest conditions.

Sea Temperature & Swimming Conditions

The Mediterranean off Sotogrande warms to a pleasant 22–24°C in July. That's ideal for swimming, snorkelling, and paddleboarding without a wetsuit. The water is clearest in the morning before the breeze stirs up sand. Popular swimming spots include Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, and the sheltered bay at Cabopino.

If you're chartering a boat with a swim platform (all our boats have one), you can step straight into the sea. For a longer swim, anchor in 5–10 metres of water and enjoy the visibility — often 10–15 metres in July.

Best Boats for July Charters

With 20+ boats in our fleet, here are the top picks for July conditions:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) — €749/2h or €2,299/8h. A sporty flybridge with plenty of shade, ideal for couples or small families.
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) — same pricing as Astondoa. Spacious cockpit and a large swim platform for easy water access.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) — €4,719 minimum 4h, includes a free jet ski. Perfect for groups wanting speed and luxury.
  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) — great for entertaining, with a large flybridge sundeck and shaded saloon.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA. No hidden costs.

Typical July Wind Patterns

July is dominated by two winds: the levante (easterly) and the poniente (westerly). The poniente is a gentle, warm breeze — ideal for cruising. The levante can bring stronger gusts and a short chop, especially near the Strait of Gibraltar. However, in July, the levante rarely exceeds 20 knots and usually lasts only a day.

Your skipper will monitor the forecast and adjust the route accordingly. For example, if the levante blows, they'll shelter along the coast near Estepona or head north towards Marbella. If it's calm, a run down to Sotogrande's marina or even towards Gibraltar is possible.

Daylight Hours & Best Times to Sail

In July, the sun rises around 07:15 and sets around 21:30, giving you over 14 hours of daylight. The hottest part of the day is 13:00–17:00, so many charters start at 10:00 or 11:00 to enjoy cooler mornings and return by sunset.

For a full-day charter (8 hours), consider an early start at 09:00. You'll have the sea to yourself, avoid the midday heat, and can anchor for lunch before the breeze picks up. Sunset charters (18:00–21:00) are also magical, with golden light over La Concha mountain.

Routes from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande

Our boats depart from Puerto Banús, about 20 nautical miles north of Sotogrande. A typical July itinerary includes:

  • Option 1: Head south along the coast, stopping at Cabopino for a swim, then continue to Sotogrande for lunch at the marina or a beach club.
  • Option 2: Cruise to Estepona (10 NM) for a quieter anchorage, then return via Puerto Banús for a sunset view.
  • Option 3: For thrill-seekers, take the Mangusta 80 and use the included jet ski to explore hidden coves.

All routes are flexible — your skipper will adapt based on weather and your preferences.

Booking Tips for July

July is peak season, so book early. We recommend at least 2–3 weeks' notice for standard boats and 4–6 weeks for the Mangusta 80. Weekends fill first, so consider a weekday charter for more availability and quieter seas.

All our charters include everything you need — just bring your swimsuit and sunscreen. For pricing on boats not listed above (e.g., Ferretti 94, Pershing 46), contact us via WhatsApp for a tailored quote.
